Subject: Weekly slot & buffer plan — pipeline-to-fleet readout

Team —

Attaching the latest slot matrix (v6) and a small delta file that maps committed slots to expected GPU-hours for the next 90 days. Purpose: align Sales/Finance/Infra on buffer sizing for high-touch deals (primarily APX-2234 / ApexAI). Key asks this week:

- Laura: confirm deal-weighted slot start dates and any accelerated close probability for Nov/Dec.
- Ben: finalize buffer cost that Finance is comfortable carrying vs. credits for customer.
- Kim: confirm burst lead time and whether we can expose a 10% burst window for Dedicated pools for this class of deal.

Quick facts from my draft (see slot_matrix_v6.xlsx):
- ApexAI (APX-2234): requested 120 reserved slots over 12 months, tiered starting 2027-01-01, model mix: 60% conv/40% retrieval (forecasted median seq 1024).
- Conversion to GPU equivalent (A100-80GB baseline): ~38 A100-equivalent continuous slots (see commit_delta.csv calculations).
- Proposed buffer: 15% on top of committed baseline for the first 90 days; drops to 7% after ramp if utilization stabilizes.

Notes: buffers can be realized via burst credits (preferred) or temporary dedicated slots. If Finance would rather avoid carrying reserved costs, sales can offer a reduced initial commitment + ramp schedule; need to quantify impact on unit economics.

Filing: slot_matrix_v6.xlsx, commit_delta.csv attached.

-Jonas
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: slot_matrix_v6.xlsx (xlsx), commit_delta.csv (csv)

Thanks Jonas — good starting point. A few updates on the ApexAI ask after the deal team sync this morning:

1) Net new ask: ApexAI confirmed they want an earlier partial start: 40% of the slots to be available 2026-12-15 for a pilot (not full traffic). That shifts ~16 A100-equivalent slots into Dec.
2) Probability & ramp: Sales now estimates close probability at 75% by EOY if pilot goes well. Ramp to full commit (120 slots) by 2027-02-15 rather than 2027-01-01.
3) Model mix nuance: The retrieval workload will be heavier than previously modeled for the pilot (higher memory working set); please assume a 1.3x GPU utilization factor for Dec pilot.
4) Related deals: two smaller mid-market pilots (NimbusHealth, ClearSky) show signs of moving Q1; combined they represent ~18 slots. Consider pooling buffer across these three deals rather than per-deal buffers.

Action items I can own: update the deal workbook with the revised start dates + probability and produce a 'cash vs reserve' P&L delta for Finance by Friday.

Laura Bennett

Marking received. Finance perspective: a few constraints and options below.

- Carrying cost: carrying 15% buffer on a 12-month reserved commitment for ApexAI equates to roughly $72k incremental spend in Q1 (based on current price cadence).
- Tradeoffs: If Sales prefers to avoid immediate reserved cost, Finance supports a hybrid: 40% initial reserved at signed rate + 60% flexible burst credits for first 90 days (we model this as a one-time credit amortized over 3 months).
- Approval: For buffers under $100k, Treasury can approve as a controlled expense; above that we need VP-Finance sign-off (I can route).

Ask from Ben: Laura — once you publish the updated workbook, please add a scenario tab that models: (A) Full reserved + 15% buffer, (B) Hybrid reserved+burst (your suggested ramp), (C) Minimal reserved (30%) + larger burst credits. I will prep the approval path and the expected P&L impact.

Ben Carter
Head of Finance
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Weekly slot & buffer plan — pipeline-to-fleet readout

Thanks all — infra notes and feasibility: 

- Burst lead time: for Dedicated pools we need 7 business days to spin up new keyed slots with appropriate affinity. For small burst windows (<=10%) we can provide a soft-burst within 48–72 hours if the pool has slack; not guaranteed, but we can set a policy-based SLA (best-effort).
- Isolation/placement: ApexAI's retrieval-heavy pilot will require larger GPU memory instances (H100-equivalent or A100-80GB with >1.2x memory pressure). I recommend earmarking the Dec pilot for a labeled burst pool to avoid disruption to other customers.
- Monitoring & throttles: we'll configure early throttles on prefix-level caching to protect latency SLOs during pilot ramp. Marcus and I will produce a short runbook for on-call if utilization spikes.

Marcus Lin: please add infra runbook and the expected slot-to-GPU mapping for the December pilot into the Drive folder (see link).

Kimberly Park
Director, Infra Reliability
Redwood Inference
